attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors represents the product of the magnitude of one vector and the magnitude of the projection of the other vector onto it. Geometrically, it equals |A||B|cos(θ), where θ is the angle between vectors A and B. If the vectors are orthogonal (θ = 90°), their dot product is zero because cos(90°) = 0, meaning there is no projection of one vector onto the other. If the dot product is negative, it indicates that the angle between the vectors is greater than 90°, so the projection of one vector onto the other points in the opposite direction, representing a negative component along that vector.

attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors measures how much one vector extends in the direction of another. Geometrically, it equals the product of their lengths and the cosine of the angle between them: A·B = |A||B|cos(θ). When vectors are orthogonal (at 90°), their dot product is zero because cos(90°) = 0, meaning no component of one lies along the other. A negative dot product means the angle between vectors is greater than 90°, so the projection of one vector onto the other points opposite its direction, indicating a negative component along that vector.
